candidates.exact_span: A. SSM language has been included.
candidates.computation_change_reason: SSM provisions govern when insufficient-sample or non-representative conditions alter monitoring obligations and how missing or non-obtainable results are classified; different readings of what SSM requires or excuses would change whether monitoring was required and how no-result periods are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: C. Outfall 004 and all associated requirements and limits have been removed at the request of the permittee. Outfall was never constructed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Outfall 004 and its associated limits and monitoring are in scope affects which discharge points, parameters, and obligations are evaluated; treating removal as eliminating all Outfall 004 duties versus leaving residual requirements would change limit and monitoring applicability.

candidates.exact_span: D. 30 day average limit for aluminum and copper have been included.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This change introduces 30-day average limit types and parameters (aluminum and copper) whose applicable numeric limits and averaging period differ from maximum instantaneous limits; interpreting which limit form applies and whether aluminum limits appear elsewhere changes enforceable limit selection and related monitoring expectations.

candidates.exact_span: E. Cadmium monitoring and reporting requirements have been included.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Newly included cadmium monitoring and reporting establishes an obligation to monitor cadmium during applicable periods; whether this creates a standalone monitoring duty or pairs with a numeric limit in the effluent table affects both monitoring-applicability and limit-comparison rows for cadmium.

The segment lists only Outfall 001 as an operative outfall on this page; interpreting whether other outfalls remain active elsewhere or were fully removed (e.g., Outfall 004) changes which discharge points are in scope for limits, monitoring, and missing-evidence evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Because of limited data and to comply with anti-backsliding laws, the current permit establishes monitoring requirements for several metals based on data submitted in 2015.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage links monitoring requirements to 2015 characterization data and anti-backsliding constraints rather than stating explicit permit limits; reading it as establishing enforceable numeric limits versus report-only or conditionally applicable monitoring would change which measurements receive numeric compliance comparisons and which monitoring duties are deemed operative.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, because discharge is very infrequent, with the last discharge occuring more than five years ago, it is impossible to have the permittee submit data satisfying SSM because of the inability to obtain a sample to analyze.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Infrequent discharge and inability to obtain SSM-satisfying samples bear on whether monitoring was required during no-discharge periods, whether SSM exceptions apply, and whether absent data reflects documented no-discharge, excused non-sampling, or unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Copper is reported as total metals.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether copper measurements must be evaluated as total metal versus another speciation (e.g., dissolved) changes the applicable comparison basis when checking reported results against copper limits.

candidates.exact_span: The geometric means, analytical results, expressed in µg/l , of analytical results are listed below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describing the following values as geometric means of 2015 analytical results in µg/l, rather than as stated permit limits, affects whether the table supplies enforceable numeric limits or background characterization used only to set separate monitoring requirements.

The Max/Avg column labels and the mg/l default unit conflict with the preceding µg/l statement; different readings of which unit and statistic (maximum versus average) governs would change the numeric limits used for compliance comparison.

If the table values are read as enforceable limits, the 0.012 MGD maximum flow figure becomes the applicable numeric discharge limit for flow comparisons; if read as historical characterization only, no numeric flow limit would be taken from this span.

The minimum pH value sets a lower bound for numeric pH compliance if treated as a permit limit; interpreting it instead as a 2015 geometric-mean characterization would remove or alter that bound in limit-selection logic.
The maximum pH value sets an upper bound for numeric pH compliance if treated as a permit limit; alternative readings of the table as background data would change whether this bound is enforceable.

The 62.33 figure is presented under a Max column and would serve as the applicable TSS limit if the table is operative; construing it as historical effluent characterization would change whether a numeric TSS limit is available for comparison.
The 2.0 BOD value under Max would be the enforceable numeric limit if the table states permit limits; treating the table as 2015 characterization would alter BOD limit applicability.

The cadmium entry pairs a numeric value with a footnote marker whose meaning is not in this segment; different readings of *1 (limit basis, averaging, reporting-only, or units) would change the enforceable cadmium limit and associated monitoring duty.

The copper Max value conflicts with the separate change noting a 30-day average limit; whether 0.006 is a maximum instantaneous limit, a characterization statistic, or superseded by a 30-day average limit changes the applicable copper limit for comparison.

ND may denote non-detect in characterization data or signal absence of a stated numeric limit; interpreting it as a compliance limit versus a no-data/non-detect state changes whether lead receives numeric limit comparison and how missing lead results are classified.

The mercury value and *2 footnote marker (undefined in this segment) may establish a numeric limit, a reporting threshold, or a monitoring trigger; unresolved footnote meaning would change mercury limit selection and whether mercury monitoring is required.
